traits.crown_see_through.note: Imagekit woody-forms photo measures (2026-10-19, plantgen-claude project-files/image-data/woody-forms-2026-10-19/CROWNS.md): median sky inside the crown outline of 2 side-view photographs of leafy open-grown trees, plantc measure-mask: 0.11.

traits.leader.note: Sargent's Manual (sargent-1922, p. 161): 'a short trunk ... slender pendulous branches forming a rather compact round-topped shapely head'.

traits.branch_posture.note: Sargent's Manual (sargent-1922, p. 161): 'slender pendulous branches forming a rather compact round-topped shapely head'.

appearance.twig.note: Sargent's Manual (2nd ed. 1922, read at the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17), as Salix Scouleriana: "stout branchlets marked by scattered yellow lenticels, coated when they first appear with pale early deciduous pubescence, becoming bright yellow or dark orange color, and in their second year dark red-brown". Colour chosen by eye between dark orange and red-brown.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_max_m.note: FEIS's Scouler's willow review (Anderson 2001, read 2026-10-15): "generally a shrub, reaching 6 to 35 feet (2-10.6 m) in height"; "occasionally grows as a tree and may reach 65 feet (20 m)".

traits.leaf_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it.

traits.leaf_habit.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as the FEIS review read does not say it in words.

traits.sexual_system.note: FEIS's Scouler's willow review (Anderson 2001, read 2026-10-15): "A dioecious plant".

traits.inflorescence.note: FEIS's Scouler's willow review (Anderson 2001, read 2026-10-15): "Aments, expanding before or with leaves and quickly deciduous": catkins.

traits.fruit_type.note: FEIS's Scouler's willow review (Anderson 2001, read 2026-10-15): "a capsule 5-8 mm long with dense, short hairs".

traits.fruit_size_m.note: FEIS's Scouler's willow review (Anderson 2001, read 2026-10-15): capsule "5-8 mm long".

traits.flowering_months.note: A model estimate (confidence high), the catkins open before or with the leaves (FEIS, Anderson 2001); the months are the model's.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as the FEIS review read gives no months.

allometry.note: 6 m at 25 years in the open, within FEIS's 2-10.6 m (Anderson 2001). Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: By eye, after FEIS (Anderson 2001): smooth to flaky grey bark; leaves obovate to oblanceolate, mostly untoothed, with paler undersides. The bark colour after Sargent's Manual (2nd ed. 1922, read at the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17), as Salix Scouleriana: "Bark thin, dark brown slightly tinged with red, and divided into broad flat ridges"; a dark grey-brown between it and FEIS's grey, chosen by eye, where a pale grey had made its limbs the lightest thing in the crown.

traits.height_typical_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L2920474), as no source read gives it.

traits.leaf_apex.note: FNA, Salix scouleriana (read 2026-10-18): the largest mid-shoot blades have an acuminate, convex (obtuse) or rounded tip.
